title: Who are the Zizians?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck give a near-real-time true crime overview of the Zizians, a group centered on Ziz, a trans woman and self-described Sith who emerged from the Bay Area rationalist community. The episode traces her move from Alaska to Berkeley, the Rationalist Fleet on boats at the Berkeley Marina, the 2019 Sefar retreat protest and its arrests, the Vallejo property dispute with Curtis Lind (stabbing and shooting), the 2022 Pennsylvania murders of Michelle Zajko's parents, the 2025 Vermont Border Patrol shootout, and the Maryland arrests. The hosts repeatedly stress that the allegations are unproven and that the case is ongoing.

entities.name: Pennsylvania murders of Richard and Rita Zajko

segments.title: Opening and introduction of Ziz
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Zizians as a timely true crime topic, with a caveat that the allegations are unproven and that many members are trans. They introduce Ziz, born in 1991 in Fairbanks, Alaska, with a strong academic and internship background.

segments.title: Rationalist movement and Eliezer Yudkowsky
segments.summary: The rationalist community, centered in Silicon Valley, is described along with AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky, the AI alignment problem, the Less Wrong blog, MIRI, CFAR, and the link to effective altruism.

segments.title: Ziz's radical views and Sith persona
segments.summary: Ziz wrote radical content on her blog, called herself a Sith, took the name from the story Worm, and stood out for intense veganism and animal rights devotion, which led to a split from the rationalists.

segments.title: Rationalist Fleet on the Berkeley Marina
segments.summary: Ziz and Gwen Danielson lived on sailboats in the Berkeley Marina to cut living costs, forming the Rationalist Fleet, which bought an old tugboat, Caleb, that proved unmanageable.

segments.title: Recruits, blog following, and unihemispheric sleep
segments.summary: New members including Emma Baranian, Alex Leatham, Michelle Zajko and Alice Monday joined through Ziz's blog. The group explored vegan transhumanism and unihemispheric sleep experiments, which critics linked to sleep deprivation and suicides.

segments.title: Break with rationalists and 2019 Sefar retreat protest
segments.summary: The group accused CFAR/MIRI of paying off a blackmailer. At the 2019 Sefar retreat, four members wearing masks and robes blocked exits, prompting a report of an active shooter and their arrest on false imprisonment and child endangerment charges. They were later banned from rationalist spaces.

segments.title: Vallejo property and Curtis Lind stabbing
segments.summary: The group moved to Curtis Lind's land in Vallejo, California. Neighbors were alarmed. In 2022 Ziz's death was reported after a boating accident and Gwen Danielson died by suicide. After a COVID eviction moratorium ended, Curtis Lind was stabbed and shot; Alex Leatham and Suri Dal were charged, and Emma Baranian was killed. Ziz and Gwen were later found to be alive.

segments.title: Pennsylvania murders and Ziz's arrest in Vermont
segments.summary: Michelle Zajko and Alice Monday moved to Vermont with Daniel Blank. Zajko's parents Richard and Rita were shot in Pennsylvania on December 31 2022. Police found cash and prepaid phones, and Ziz was arrested and held for five months on misdemeanor charges, then failed to appear at trial in December 2023.

segments.title: Vermont Border Patrol shootout and Curtis Lind's killing
segments.summary: Olivia Bachholt, Maximilian Snyder and Milo Younblood joined the group. In January 2025 Bachholt and Younblood were in Vermont, where a Border Patrol firefight killed agent David Malland and Bachholt. Snyder allegedly killed Curtis Lind days earlier before he could testify.

segments.title: Maryland arrests and current status
segments.summary: In February 2025 Ziz, Zajko and Blank were arrested in Maryland after guns were found in trucks. Those charged are in custody; Zajko has written an open letter denying involvement. The hosts note the case is ongoing and that Caleb sank in the marina.

segments.title: Listener mail from James on jaywalking and pagan
segments.summary: A listener notes that words like pagan and jaywalking have origins in slurs, and suggests car-related rules in the early 20th century as a reason for jaywalking's creation. Hosts recall an episode on car dominance.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and sign off with the show's contact information.
